extracted.intended_audience: general readers; researchers and journalists interested in social media, disinformation, and online journalism
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article profiling a Brazilian social-media account (@Choquei) that summarizes its history, content style, operational practices, reception, and controversies (including misinformation incidents).

rubrics_metrics.name: All-caps urgent-style headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes news in short, urgent-style headlines in all-caps at the beginning of each post to define the subject such as "serious" and "urgent".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This headline format functions to quickly define the subject and convey urgency; it is typically placed at the start of the post and is part of the 'Choquei style' that increases attention and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of siren emoji to convey urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: An emoji of a siren (🚨) is an element used at the beginning of Choquei's posts to attract attention and convey a sense of urgency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The siren emoji is combined with all-caps headlines and other attention-grabbing devices to signal breaking or serious news; it is an explicit stylistic choice for immediacy and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provocative language and black comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Posts often use provocative language and black comedy, sparking intense debates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provocative tone can drive engagement and debate but also increases risk of backlash, reputational harm, and ethical issues (example: mocking a victim prior to a subsequent tragedy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of photos/videos to complement or sensationalize
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses a photo or video, sometimes two, in posts to complement or reinforce the narrative and capture attention; in some instances images appear to be used to sensationalize the news, even when they have no direct connection to the reported event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia is leveraged to strengthen stories and engagement; anti-patterns include using decontextualized or manipulated images, which have led to debunking by fact-checkers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy-and-paste reposting from other outlets without context or fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Fast-paced information shared in a "copy and paste" manner, where almost all of the content published is based on reporting from other media outlets often without providing context, crediting sources or fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operational approach prioritizes speed and volume over independent verification and has been linked to accusations of fake news and multiple debunked posts; it represents a trade-off between rapid dissemination and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous language that amplifies minor aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses ambiguous language that amplifies minor aspects of a story while omitting full context; phrases such as "maximum alert" are also employed to intensify the perceived seriousness of the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity and sensational phrasing increase perceived gravity and engagement but can mislead audiences by omitting clarifying context and nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting frequency: irregular, volume-driven cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting frequency of the profile is irregular — "We don't have a quota. Some days we make 40, 50, 60 posts. Other days it doesn't reach 10. It depends daily on what's happening in the world, and there's no fixed routine either."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-volume bursts during news events maximize reach; organizationally this required staff working shifts (six blocks per day). The irregular cadence supports rapid coverage but complicates verification workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark engagement metrics for success
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers a Twitter post successful when it reaches 10,000 likes, while on Instagram the benchmark was 100,000 likes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numeric targets function as internal success metrics that guide editorial and commercial decisions (e.g., bonuses, advertiser appeal) and incentivize attention-maximizing tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for reposting from 'reliable outlets' rather than independent fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Raphael states that fact-checking takes time, and for this reason the page prefers to repost content from "reliable outlets" as a way to maintain both speed and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a pragmatic editorial rule balancing speed and perceived credibility; however, reliance on other outlets can still propagate errors if original sources are misinterpreted or outdated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational staffing and shift coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Team composition and schedules: the account's team included content producers who operated in shifts divided into time blocks across two daily periods, totaling six blocks per day; each employee covered one time block while the owner coordinated operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing and shift structure enable near-continuous posting and rapid response to events; compensation combined fixed salary and bonuses for high-performing posts, aligning staff incentives with engagement outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive content focus based on audience traction
rubrics_metrics.description: The account shifted content focus multiple times (e.g., adding international or economic news) as certain topics gained traction with followers; these changes affected posting style and reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapting topical focus to what 'gains traction' is an editorial strategy for growth; it can broaden audience but also changes risk profile (e.g., moving into political coverage brought scrutiny and misinformation accusations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unverified claims and early reporting during breaking events (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Published unverified claims, hasty translations, and blunt/abbreviated phrases during breaking events; examples include sharing false claims about bodies in Ukrainian streets and early posts about election outcomes prior to official confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These behaviors have led to posts being debunked by fact-checkers and serious consequences (e.g., public backlash, contribution to real-world harm); they are presented as risky anti-patterns rather than recommended practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization tied to follower counts and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The account became financially viable after reaching 100,000 followers; early advertisers were local stores and later major brands; political bias did not necessarily deter advertisers according to the owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follower thresholds and engagement benchmarks directly influence commercial opportunities, shaping content incentives toward attention-maximizing formats and sensationalism.
